question: What is the main purpose of the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: To test basic skills in controlling a commercial vehicle and judging its position relative to other objects
choice_b: To test the vehicle's mechanical condition
choice_c: To test knowledge of traffic laws
choice_d: To test the applicant's ability to read a map
explanation: The manual states the Basic Control Skills test shows basic skills in controlling a commercial vehicle and judging its position in relation to other objects.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 12, Basic Control Skills Test

question: What must an applicant do when entering or exiting the vehicle during a backing exercise?
choice_a: Jump down from the cab facing away from the vehicle
choice_b: Set the parking brake, place the vehicle in neutral, and maintain three points of contact while facing the vehicle
choice_c: Exit quickly without setting the parking brake to save time
choice_d: Leave the engine running and the door open
explanation: The manual requires setting the parking brake, placing the vehicle in neutral, and safely exiting/entering while facing the vehicle and keeping three points of contact at all times.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 12, Basic Control Skills Test

topic: Basic Control Skills Test - Scoring: Looks
question: What action during a backing exercise will be scored as a "look"?
choice_a: Checking mirrors while remaining seated
choice_b: Opening the door or moving from a seated position while in physical control of the vehicle
explanation: The manual states that opening the door or moving from a seated position while in physical control of the vehicle will be scored as a look.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 12.1, Scoring - Looks

question: What must an applicant do if the examiner raises their hand during an exercise?
choice_a: Accelerate to complete the exercise faster
choice_b: Stop and return the vehicle within the exercise boundary lines
explanation: The manual instructs that if the examiner raises their hand, the applicant must stop and return the vehicle within the exercise boundary lines.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 12, Basic Control Skills Test

topic: Basic Control Skills Test - Scoring: Pull-Ups
question: In which two exercises can an applicant receive a scored "pull-up"?
choice_a: All four exercises equally
choice_b: Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing) and Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing)
choice_c: Exercise 1 (Forward Stop) and Exercise 3 (Forward Offset Tracking)
explanation: The manual specifies that pull-ups are scored during Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing) and Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing).
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 12.1, Scoring - Pull-Ups

topic: Basic Control Skills Test - Scoring: Encroachments
question: Which of the following would NOT count as an encroachment if it touches or crosses a boundary line or cone?
choice_a: The vehicle's door or fender mirror
choice_b: The vehicle's rear bumper
choice_d: The vehicle's side panel below mirror height
explanation: The manual excludes the vehicle's mirrors (door or fender) and unique vehicle parts at or higher than door mirror height from counting as encroachments; other vehicle parts touching a boundary do count.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 12.1, Scoring - Encroachments

topic: Basic Control Skills Test - Scoring: Looks
question: How many free looks is an applicant allowed on Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing)?
choice_a: Zero
choice_b: Two
explanation: The manual allows a maximum of one free look on Exercise 2, Straight-Line Backing, to check the position of the vehicle.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 12.1, Scoring - Looks

topic: Basic Control Skills Test - Scoring: Looks
question: How many free looks is an applicant allowed on Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing)?
choice_a: One
choice_b: Three
explanation: The manual allows a maximum of two free looks on Exercise 4, Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 12.1, Scoring - Looks

topic: Basic Control Skills Test - Scoring: Final Position
question: After completing a Basic Control Skills exercise, what three actions should the applicant take?
choice_a: Set the parking brake, place the vehicle in neutral or park, and sound the horn
choice_b: Turn off the engine, exit the vehicle, and wait for instructions
choice_c: Activate the four-way flashers and honk twice
choice_d: Roll down the window and wave to the examiner
explanation: The manual instructs that after completing an exercise, the applicant should set the parking brake, place the vehicle in neutral or park, and sound the horn.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 12.1, Scoring - Final Position

question: In Exercise 1 (Forward Stop), how many times may the applicant stop while driving through the alley?
choice_a: As many times as needed
choice_b: Only once
explanation: The manual states the applicant may stop only once when driving forward through the alley and stopping within the box.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 12.2.1, Exercise 1: Forward Stop

question: In Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing), how far must the applicant back the vehicle?
choice_a: Until the rear of the vehicle touches a wall
choice_b: Exactly 10 feet regardless of cone placement
choice_c: Straight through the alley until the front of the vehicle has cleared the last set of cones
choice_d: Until instructed to stop by a passenger
explanation: The manual instructs backing straight through the alley until the front of the vehicle has cleared the last set of cones at the far end of the alley.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 12.2.2, Exercise 2: Straight Line Backing

question: What is the applicant NOT allowed to do during Exercise 3 (Forward Offset Tracking)?
choice_a: Steer to the left
choice_b: Stop, back up, or exit the vehicle
explanation: The manual states the applicant is not allowed to stop, back up, or exit the vehicle during this exercise; if they stop, the exercise is over.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 12.2.3, Exercise 3: Forward Offset Tracking

question: In Exercise 3, where must the applicant keep the right-most rear tire while tracking forward?
choice_a: In the center of the alley only
choice_b: Between the cone and the line
explanation: The manual specifies keeping the right-most rear tire between the cone and the line while moving forward without stopping.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 12.2.3, Exercise 3: Forward Offset Tracking

question: In Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing), how close must the rear of the vehicle come to the rear of the alley?
choice_a: Within 10 feet
choice_b: Within 1 foot
explanation: The manual requires bringing the rear-most part of the vehicle within three (3) feet of the rear of the alley, stopping in the three-foot box.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 12.2.4, Exercise 4: Reverse Offset Backing

question: How many free pull-ups and vehicle exits (looks) are allowed during Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing)?
choice_a: One free pull-up and one exit
choice_b: Unlimited pull-ups and exits
choice_c: Two free pull-ups and a maximum of two exits
choice_d: No free pull-ups or exits allowed
explanation: The manual allows two free pull-ups and a maximum of two vehicle exits to check around the vehicle during Exercise 4.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 12.2.4, Exercise 4: Reverse Offset Backing

question: According to the manual, what must an applicant do to pass the on-road driving test?
choice_a: Complete the route in under 15 minutes
choice_b: Drive at the posted speed limit at all times, even if unsafe
choice_c: Complete the test without an accident or moving violation, while wearing a safety belt and obeying traffic signs, signals, and laws
choice_d: Avoid using turn signals to reduce distraction
explanation: The manual lists wearing a safety belt, obeying all traffic signs/signals/laws, and completing the test without an accident or moving violation as core requirements.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 13, On-road Driving

question: What happens if the on-road test route does not include certain traffic situations, such as a railroad crossing?
choice_a: The examiner skips scoring for that category
choice_b: The applicant automatically fails
choice_c: The applicant may be asked to simulate the traffic situation by describing what they would do
choice_d: The test is rescheduled for another day
explanation: The manual states that if the test route lacks certain traffic situations, the applicant may be asked to simulate them by telling the examiner what they are or would be doing.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 13, On-road Driving

question: What is considered "unsafe coasting" during a turn, according to the manual?
choice_a: The vehicle being out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of the vehicle
choice_b: Using a turn signal for more than 3 seconds
explanation: The manual defines unsafe coasting as the vehicle being out of gear for more than the length of the vehicle while slowing for a turn.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 13.1.1, Turns

question: If stopping behind another vehicle before a turn, where should the applicant stop?
choice_a: Where they can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead (a safe gap)
choice_b: Anywhere within the marked lane
choice_c: As close as possible to the vehicle ahead
choice_d: At least one full vehicle length plus 10 feet back
explanation: The manual instructs stopping where the driver can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead, maintaining a safe gap.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 13.1.1, Turns

question: While driving through an intersection, what must the applicant avoid doing?
choice_a: Changing lanes while proceeding through the intersection
choice_b: Yielding to pedestrians
explanation: The manual states the applicant must not change lanes while proceeding through an intersection.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 13.1.2, Intersections

question: What must the applicant avoid doing while any part of the vehicle is within a railroad crossing?
choice_a: Checking traffic in all directions
choice_b: Stopping, changing gears, passing another vehicle, or changing lanes
choice_d: Keeping hands on the steering wheel
explanation: The manual states the driver must not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of the vehicle is in the crossing.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 13.1.8, Railroad Crossing

question: If driving a bus, school bus, or placarded vehicle, how close to the nearest rail must the vehicle stop before crossing railroad tracks?
choice_a: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail
choice_b: Exactly 100 feet from the nearest rail
explanation: The manual requires stopping within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail for buses, school buses, and placarded vehicles.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 13.1.8, Railroad Crossing

question: When resuming from a stop-and-start maneuver on the side of the road, what should the applicant do before the vehicle moves?
choice_a: Immediately accelerate to highway speed
choice_b: Not turn the wheel before the vehicle moves, and check traffic first
choice_d: Turn the steering wheel toward traffic first
explanation: The manual instructs not to turn the wheel before the vehicle moves, and to check traffic from all directions, especially the left, before pulling back into traffic.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 13.1.6, Stop and Start

question: According to the manual's general driving behavior guidance, what must a driver do when shifting an unsynchronized manual transmission?
choice_a: Pop the clutch quickly
choice_b: Rev the engine heavily before each shift
choice_c: Coast with the clutch depressed between gears
explanation: The manual states that if the vehicle has an unsynchronized manual transmission, the driver must double-clutch when shifting, and should not rev or lug the engine.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 13.1.11(A), Clutch Usage

question: According to the manual's lane usage guidance, where should a driver finish a right turn on a multiple lane road?
choice_a: In the left-most lane
choice_b: In the center lane
choice_d: In whichever lane has less traffic
explanation: The manual states that a driver should finish a right turn in the right-most (curb) lane.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 13.1.14(D), Lane Usage
